question: In a 68-year-old patient with new onset headache, pain and prolonged morning stiffness in scapular and pelvic girdles of several weeks of evolution that presents unilateral bruising of sudden onset, what treatment among the following would establish before confirming the diagnosis?

options.opb: Methylprednisolone 1 g i.v. daily for three days.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "68-year-old patient with new onset headache" -> "possible inflammatory condition" -> "consider giant cell arteritis" -> "bruising suggests possible vasculitis" -> "high-dose corticosteroids indicated" -> "Methylprednisolone 1 g i.v. daily for three days" -> 85%

CHAIN: "68-year-old patient with prolonged morning stiffness" -> "suggests polymyalgia rheumatica" -> "associated with giant cell arteritis" -> "unilateral bruising indicates possible systemic involvement" -> "initiate treatment with corticosteroids" -> "Prednisone 10 mg daily v.o." -> 80%

CHAIN: "68-year-old patient with scapular and pelvic girdle pain" -> "indicates possible inflammatory myopathy" -> "unilateral bruising raises suspicion for vasculitis" -> "high-dose corticosteroids may be necessary" -> "Methylprednisolone 1 g i.v. daily for three days" -> 90%

CHAIN: "68-year-old patient with new onset headache and stiffness" -> "consider differential diagnosis including vasculitis" -> "unilateral bruising suggests systemic involvement" -> "initiate treatment with immunosuppressive therapy" -> "Cyclophosphamide i.v. 1 g / m2" -> "unclear if immediate treatment is warranted" -> 70%

CHAIN: "68-year-old patient with symptoms of headache and stiffness" -> "possible autoimmune condition" -> "unilateral bruising indicates possible severe inflammation" -> "consider anti-TNF therapy" -> "Infliximab i.v. 3 mg / Kg" -> "not first-line treatment before diagnosis" -> 60%
enhanced_information: In a 68-year-old patient with new onset headache, prolonged morning stiffness, and unilateral bruising, there is a strong suspicion of giant cell arteritis (GCA) or polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR) with possible systemic involvement. High-dose corticosteroids are indicated as a first-line treatment to prevent complications such as vision loss associated with GCA. The reasoning for Methylprednisolone 1 g i.v. daily for three days aligns with the consensus that immediate high-dose corticosteroid therapy is warranted in suspected GCA. Prednisone 10 mg daily is less aggressive and may not be sufficient for urgent cases. Cyclophosphamide is not indicated as an initial treatment for GCA or PMR, and Infliximab is not first-line therapy before confirming the diagnosis. Therefore, the best option is Methylprednisolone 1 g i.v. daily for three days.
analysis: The patient's symptoms, including new onset headache, prolonged morning stiffness in the scapular and pelvic girdles, and unilateral bruising, raise a strong suspicion for giant cell arteritis (GCA) or polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR) with possible systemic involvement. In cases of suspected GCA, immediate treatment with high-dose corticosteroids is critical to prevent complications such as vision loss. The consensus in the medical community supports the use of high-dose intravenous corticosteroids, specifically Methylprednisolone 1 g i.v. daily for three days, as the first-line treatment before confirming the diagnosis. Prednisone 10 mg daily is insufficient for urgent cases, while Cyclophosphamide and Infliximab are not appropriate initial treatments for GCA or PMR. Therefore, the best-supported option is Methylprednisolone 1 g i.v. daily for three days, aligning with established guidelines for managing suspected GCA.
